reasoning: The server logic is nearly identical and sound in both. A passes every check and detects right-drag camera turns correctly by adding up mouse Delta. B fails StyLua on its own new lines, and its position-based drag check doesn't catch locked-cursor camera turns. B's Destroying cleanup is a nice extra but doesn't make up for those.

criteria.note: Changes stay in BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau in the existing style, adding small helpers (getRootPart, isRateLimited, raycastFromScreen) and no new framework.
A server table `placedBlocks[part] = {OwnerUserId, Cell}` is checked against player.UserId, and nothing the client sends is trusted.

Checks typeof Instance, requires a server record (so only placed blocks qualify), checks reach and the shared rate limit, and clears occupied; there's no explicit IsDescendantOf, but the record lookup does the same job.
MouseButton2 adds up InputChanged Delta to tell a click from a camera drag, TouchLongPress Begin with one touch removes, and gameProcessed input is ignored; placing is unchanged.
All checks pass, placing still works, and the changes are limited to the two files.
Changes stay in the two existing files in their style, with no new structure.
A server `blocks[part]` record holds OwnerUserId; the attribute is used only as a client hint, and the server trusts its own table.
Checks typeof and the record, then rate and reach, clears occupied, and a Destroying handler frees the cell however the block goes away.

MouseButton2 is checked by press-to-release position and a 0.3s window; because the cursor is locked during a drag, position doesn't catch camera turns and only the time limit helps; long press and gameProcessed handling are correct.
Works and stays in scope, but StyLua fails on its own new lines (the rightClickStart assignment and the long onTouchLongPress signature).

strengths: Uses mouse Delta to detect right-drag camera turns, which matches how Roblox locks the cursor
One rate-limit budget shared by placing and removing
weaknesses: The placedBlocks/occupied entries aren't cleared if a block is destroyed some other way
Fires removal without a client-side ownership pre-check (harmless)

strengths: A Destroying hook keeps occupied consistent
The client pre-checks the owner attribute, so it skips requests the server would refuse
weaknesses: StyLua check fails on its own code
Telling a right-click from a camera drag relies on position, which doesn't change during a locked-cursor drag
